ruling.recommended_action: Refer to Trust & Safety human review: preserve the in-app chat, call records and GPS log for trip T-2024; interview/hold the driver account pending review; per SAFE-4 the driver (accused party) may be interim-suspended from trip acceptance until a human reviewer determines whether a safety violation occurred. Fare element separately: the quote and trip-start multiplier are both 1.3x and the actual fare ($11.81) is below the $12.31 quote, so no surge refund arises on the fare_dispute head.
ruling.reasoning:
SAFETY SCREEN: The complaint states that when the rider questioned the fare the driver said "he knows where I live and I had better just pay," and that she "felt unsafe for the rest of the ride." Read in context, this is not a pickup arrangement or idle remark — it is an implicit threat using knowledge of the rider's home to suppress a fare query, i.e. intimidation and a statement causing a rider to feel unsafe (SAFE-1), and the rider's own words assert a continuing perception of danger during the trip (SAFE-2 indicators). Under SAFE-1/SAFE-3 I cannot rule the merits on this record: the case must go to human review, and no fault may be assigned to either party here. Note that the accused driver's account cannot be tested against the chat because the chat log on file (only the pickup messages at 08:43:55 and 08:44:35) does not contain the exchange the rider quotes — the threatening statement itself is not in the produced record, so the record is also incomplete for adjudicating it; this reinforces escalation rather than a merits ruling.

FARE ELEMENT (recorded for the file, not decided as a ruling): the surge complaint itself is arithmetically not made out. The quote was at a 1.3x multiplier (surgeable subtotal $8.51, surge amount $2.55, total $12.31) and the trip-start multiplier in the surge log is also 1.3x with surge_activated_at null, so the multiplier never rose (SURGE-1 quote lock satisfied; SURGE-2 "unchanged" row would apply and the quoted fare stands). The actual fare billed is $11.81 — lower than the $12.31 quote — and its build-up is base $3.90 + distance $3.29 + time $0.93 = $8.12 surgeable × 1.3x = $10.56 + booking fee $1.25 = $11.81, with $0.00 tolls. No surge differential exists, so no SURGE-2 refund would arise; the rider's belief that a new 1.3x surge was imposed is not borne out by the record.

ROUTE ELEMENT: actual distance 2.33 km is slightly SHORT of the recommended 2.386 km (deviation −0.056 km, within the 1 km RD-1 tolerance, and below the 0.2 km noise floor), so no route-deviation refund arises either. The GPS trace on RIVER VALLEY ROAD (08:48:35), CLEMENCEAU AVENUE, OXLEY RISE, EBER ROAD, DEVONSHIRE ROAD and ORCHARD LINK tracks the optimal route's roads, with no traffic events logged.

EVIDENCE STATUS: insufficient for a merits ruling — the material chat the rider relies on (and any call record) is missing, so the safety allegation cannot be evidenced either way; missing records favour neither party. Escalate.
ruling.escalation_reason: Safety screen triggered (SAFE-1/SAFE-2): complaint alleges intimidation and a felt-safety issue; under SAFE-3 the AI may not rule, assign fault or recommend an outcome. Additionally, evidence for a merits ruling is insufficient (TH-4): the material chat exchange is missing from the record and no call recording exists, so neither the safety allegation nor the driver's account can be tested.

element_findings.element: Surge notice requirement (SURGE-1: new multiplier, revised fare, free cancellation)
element_findings.reason: No surge notice was sent at all. However the multiplier did not rise between quote (1.3x) and trip start (1.3x), so no notice was required; the non-notification is therefore immaterial and yields no refund.
Actual fare is $11.81 vs quote $12.31; the whole difference runs in the rider's favour and is not attributable to a multiplier change. Differential = $0.00.
Actual − recommended = 2.33 − 2.386 = −0.056 km, within the 1 km tolerance (and below the 0.2 km noise floor). No refundable deviation.
The complaint contains an implicit threat tied to knowledge of the rider's home and an express statement of feeling unsafe during the ride; the case must escalate and must not be ruled on its merits.

rejected_claims.reason: Not made out on the record: quote multiplier and trip-start multiplier are both 1.3x (surge_activated_at null) and the actual fare $11.81 is below the $12.31 quote, so no surge differential exists under SURGE-1/SURGE-2. Recorded for the human reviewer, not ruled on, because the case escalates on safety grounds.

safety_basis: Rider complaint: driver said 'he knows where I live and I had better just pay' when questioned about the fare — implicit threat/intimidation using knowledge of the rider's home address
Rider complaint: 'I felt unsafe for the rest of the ride' — stated perception of danger during the trip
The threatening chat exchange quoted by the rider is not present in the produced chat log (only pickup messages recorded), so the allegation is unrebutted and unverifiable on this record
ruling.evidence_gap: The chat log contains only the two pickup messages (08:43:55 rider, 08:44:35 driver); the fare-dispute exchange the rider quotes — including the alleged threat and any driver response — is absent from the record, and there is no call record. The safety allegation therefore cannot be verified or refuted from the produced evidence.
